# A lower bound of a product of two limbs

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_down_1` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A lower bound of $a b$, a number of `T` within 1 step of its rounding down, and that rounding itself where the claims say so (below):

$$r \le a b.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`mul_down_entry`](mul_down_entry.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r \le a b$, and $r$ is $\mathrm{RD}(a b)$ or at most 1 step of the format below it: a bound on that side of the exact value, at most 1 number of the format beyond its rounding down.
- $r = \mathrm{RD}(a b)$: the largest number of the format not above $a b$, when $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_down_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/DirectedProd.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/DirectedProd.v), against `mul_down_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_down_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition mul_down_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let r := mul_down_1 emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r <= (a * b) /\ pred radix2 (FLT_exp emin prec) (RD emin prec (a * b)) <= r /\
  (((a * b) = 0 \/ bpow radix2 (2 * prec - 1) * eta emin <= Rabs (a * b)) -> r = RD emin prec (a * b)).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $b$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

and then:

- If every operand is finite: $r \le a b$, and $r$ is at most 1 step of `T` below the largest number of `T` not above $a b$, which is $\Omega$ when $a b > \Omega$ and $-\infty$ when $a b < -\Omega$ (a step below $-\Omega$ gives $-\infty$).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $r = a b$, as `T` computes it.
- If every operand is finite and $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$: $r$ is the largest number of `T` not above $a b$, or $-\infty$ when $a b < -\Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $r = a b$, as `T` computes it.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `mul_down_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeDirectedProd.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeDirectedProd.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_down_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `mul_down_1_correct` and `mul_down_1_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** two_prod and the sign of its error term (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_down_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_down_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_prod`](two_prod.md).

```
# A lower bound of a b, for every pair of finite numbers (milestone2.md, "Rounding a product down
# and up"): RD(a b) when a b = 0 or |a b| >= P = 2^(2p-1) eta, the threshold above which the error
# of a product is a number of the format; below it, RD(a b) or the number of the format before it.
# The listing steps down when the computed error of two_prod is negative, or when the product is
# below P and the computed error is zero, which below P proves nothing. A zero factor, recognized
# on the operands, returns the rounded product itself. The constant is P, eta / (2 u^2), exact.
# The sign of a nonzero computed error is trusted: two_prod is evaluated with its FMA, never through
# its constant-evaluation variant, whose error term below P can have the other sign. So the kernel
# is not constexpr in this milestone (it has an fms). An infinite or NaN operand gives the product
# of IEEE 754.
# The public building block kairn::mul_down calls mul_down_entry, which guards the operands first
# (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation).

(p, e) = two_prod(a, b)
ap     = abs(p)
bd     = lt(ap, const up(eta/(2*u^2)))
ez     = eq(e, 0)
un     = and(bd, ez)
n      = lt(e, 0)
sd     = or(n, un)
pp     = pred(p)
d      = select(sd, pp, p)
za     = eq(a, 0)
zb     = eq(b, 0)
zz     = or(za, zb)
r      = select(zz, p, d)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#mul_down_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 416 404 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
